","updateAuthor":{"accountId":"70121:67e840f4-926c-4a39-9345-29bad2b38e0a","displayName":"Jason Robinson","active":false,"timeZone":"America/New_York","accountType":"atlassian"},"created":"2026-05-08T12:13:42.143-0400","updated":"2026-05-08T12:13:42.143-0400","jsdPublic":true},{"id":"3124768","author":{"accountId":"qm:77071153-8149-425d-9cc5-2ef53c35a3bd:4226ff2a-8f1f-4506-b809-3adf6a8626df","emailAddress":"cindy_coreas@tjxcanada.ca","displayName":"Cindy Coreas","active":true,"timeZone":"America/New_York","accountType":"customer"},"body":"

Hi Jason, I’ve tried removing the quotation marks, and it does seem to export the correct result count. However, the reason I initially used them is because some field users need to filter very specific results in the reports.

In this ‘True’ example, without quotation marks, the filter returns all results containing the word ‘True.’

Another example is register numbers: if they want to isolate only Register 13, the only way to do that is by entering “13.” Otherwise, searching for 13 (without quotation marks) returns all results containing that number (see below).

","updateAuthor":{"accountId":"qm:77071153-8149-425d-9cc5-2ef53c35a3bd:4226ff2a-8f1f-4506-b809-3adf6a8626df","emailAddress":"cindy_coreas@tjxcanada.ca","displayName":"Cindy Coreas","active":true,"timeZone":"America/New_York","accountType":"customer"},"created":"2026-05-08T13:26:32.594-0400","updated":"2026-05-08T13:26:32.594-0400","jsdPublic":true},{"id":"3124841","author":{"accountId":"70121:67e840f4-926c-4a39-9345-29bad2b38e0a","displayName":"Jason Robinson","active":false,"timeZone":"America/New_York","accountType":"atlassian"},"body":"

Hi @Cindy Coreas

Good point on the filtering scenarios.

What if we extend the filter conditions to mirror the Parameters panel (see attached)

— each row would have a field, an operator (Match, Contains, Equal to, etc.),

a value, and a toggle to enable or disable it? That way users get explicit control

over exact vs partial matching without needing quotation marks.

I've tried it out using Match, Contains, and Equal as optional parameters and it seems to work well.

Would you be able to give it a try and let me know what you think?

Thanks,
Jason

Hi @Aimee Wadsworth - I worked with Cindy on a call and I determined this is a bug in the application. Basically when you get results - you can export. If you use a filter without ““ - it exports only the filtered selection. But if you add a filter with ““ such as “345” - it filters, but then the export returns 0 results. I had a few people try it and I tried another production system, and it was the same. The expected result would be the export of the filtered results in the ““. I think this needs to go to product or engineering. Thank you, Jim
